decision.rationale: A compact device-only layer around the existing framework-neutral C++ core. Tauri and the shared studio stay intact; production output uses WASAPI/CoreAudio/PulseAudio/ALSA. The null backend is explicit test infrastructure, never a production fallback.

candidates.license: AGPLv3 or commercial JUCE licence; exact release terms must be reviewed before adoption
strengths: offline processing can reuse DSP code
costs: UI framework unnecessary for an existing web-based editor
candidates.maintenance: Active upstream framework; version pin and upgrade checks required
candidates.callback: high-priority audio-device callback, still requires allocation/I/O discipline in our code
candidates.reuse: C++ library boundary could serve a desktop host, mobile host and a pre-programmed native bridge

candidates.license: CPAL Apache-2.0; evaluate licences of additional DSP crates and optional platform backends independently
strengths: low-level audio I/O separated from DSP
can expose a C ABI for application/game reuse
costs: need to select or implement DSP components separately
Rust toolchain is absent in this worker environment, so no Rust performance comparison was run
candidates.maintenance: RustAudio upstream; platform feature flags and backend versions need pinning
candidates.callback: stream callback must use prepared bounded state; Rust alone does not guarantee deadline compliance
candidates.reuse: native library plus host ABI; offline rendering can use the same DSP functions

candidates.license: Upstream offers public domain or MIT No Attribution
strengths: can host an independent C++ DSP library
does not require replacing the existing editor
costs: we must provide synth/modulation/effects and higher-level session handling
mobile lifecycle, device changes and low-latency behaviour still need prototypes
candidates.maintenance: Pin an upstream revision and validate supported backends on target devices
candidates.callback: device callback only processes prepared buffers/state; no file parsing or UI calls
candidates.reuse: compact native host around the same standalone core and offline processor

prototype.input: Existing pre-midi-synth-voice v1/v2/v3 JSON is validated/prepared by a Node control-host adapter, then transferred as a bounded little-endian IPC packet. The packet is not a new musical persistence format.
prototype.output: Interleaved stereo Float32 little-endian PCM produced by C++, without Web Audio
supported: two oscillator slots: sine, triangle, square, sawtooth, 32-harmonic editable recipes
frequency-dependent band limiting with fixed recipe normalization
equal-tempered frequency/detune and prepared glide/bend curves
static lowpass/highpass (Q in dB), bandpass/notch (linear Q)
Canonical v2 modulation: all four sources, six target IDs, max 16 routes, one-pole smoothing and bounded combination
v3 compiled filter.cutoff automation before per-note modulation
prototype.unsupportedPolicy: Reject unsupported contract versions and features explicitly; never substitute another oscillator or silently bypass drive/noise/delay/legacy movement
callbackContract: Caller-owned output buffer and bounded frame count
No file/device I/O, UI calls or locks inside process()
Block-size invariance and unchanged C++ operator-new counter are executable assertions
limitations: The offline CLI remains a reference/comparison tool; desktop now also has an embedded miniaudio device host.
Not all patch v1 capabilities are implemented
No native oversampling or broad oscillator alias qualification
Native allocator and callback tests exist; physical driver underrun/thermal/suspend-resume qualification remains pending.
Desktop packaging/FFI is checked by Windows/macOS/Linux CI; no physical audio qualification is inferred.
No claim that process-per-voice CLI IPC is suitable for real-time hosting; embed the block core instead
Biquad denormals flushed below 1e-30; cross-architecture floating-point qualification pending

referenceEquations.note: Lowpass/highpass Q is in dB under the current browser contract; do not reinterpret existing saved resonance as linear Q.
